items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: think about Ella or Sarah Vaughan or somebody singing it you know, like how would I sing this?

ctx.x: It was clear to me that you understand the importance and the power of space and dynamics. Because there was a number of times, one time when you were playing — you played the melody to “Bye-Bye Blackbird.” And there was all those like holes in there. And you know Ron was playing a little bit behind you but I don’t hear people do that that much. And I wonder why you did it and I wondered is it because of this audience — it’s very quiet in there. And those silences, man, are very —

Well it’s often what you don’t play which is more powerful. You know? Giving that space in thought but also to allow the other musicians around to give him time to add his thing. So I think that’s that. I do my best, I still, of the people who leave the most space, of course Miles Davis and Wayne Shorter and those incredible, I still am trying to get to that place. Like if you see Wayne Shorter’s group play often he will just play a couple of notes and just like stand there for a long period of time. And it’s…
When you’re improvising is there such a thing as a mistake for you?
